encounters.cc: Patient is brought to the clinic by her daughter due to worsening memory loss and functional decline. Over the past 2 years, the patient has slowly lost the ability to manage her own affairs, forgotten to pay bills, and gotten lost while driving to familiar places.

lines: Patient is brought to the clinic by her daughter due to worsening memory loss and functional decline.
Over the past 2 years, the patient has slowly lost the ability to manage her own affairs, forgotten to pay bills, and gotten lost while driving to familiar places.

The patient returns to the neurology clinic for further evaluation of progressive cognitive decline, having been previously assessed in 2020 for memory concerns and managed for major depressive disorder.
She presents today accompanied by her daughter, who reports continued functional deterioration over the intervening two years.
Over the past 2 years, the patient has slowly lost the ability to manage her own affairs.
Initially, she occasionally misplaced household items and repeated the same questions.
Over the past 12 months, she has forgotten to pay bills, has gotten lost while driving to familiar places, and has had increasing trouble remembering recent conversations.
Her daughter now manages her finances and medications.
The daughter also notes personality changes.
The patient, once cheerful and outgoing, has become more withdrawn and irritable.
She frequently accuses family members of "stealing" objects that she herself misplaced.
At family gatherings, she repeats the same story several times in a short period and struggles to recall the names of distant relatives.
She sometimes forgets what she had for breakfast, though she can describe in detail events that happened 40 years ago.
Her daily functioning has been significantly affected.
She can no longer prepare complex meals, balance her checkbook, or follow television shows.
Recently, she needed help with dressing, as she put on two blouses and no pants.
She sometimes forgets to bathe unless reminded.
She is able to feed herself and use the bathroom without assistance, though she occasionally has difficulty remembering where her bedroom is in the house.
The patient denies headaches, focal weakness, numbness, or episodes of loss of consciousness.
There is no history of strokes or transient ischemic attacks.
She has no difficulty walking and denies tremors or stiffness.
She has not had visual hallucinations or fluctuations in her alertness.
- Coronary Artery Disease (status post myocardial infarction 12 years prior)
Medical history includes well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
She had a myocardial infarction 12 years ago.
She takes aspirin, enalapril, and a statin.
Family history is significant for her mother, who developed dementia in her late 70s and required nursing home care.
She does not smoke and drinks wine occasionally.
Blood pressure is 142/84 mm Hg, pulse 70/min, respirations 16/min, and temperature 36.8°C.
On examination, the patient is pleasant but disoriented to date and place.
She is neatly dressed but needs prompting to answer many questions.
She recalls 0 of 3 words after 5 minutes, is unable to copy intersecting pentagons, and cannot draw a clock face.
Naming of common objects is intact.
Cranial nerves are normal, strength and sensation are symmetric, reflexes are normal, and gait is steady.
Laboratory studies, including CBC, electrolytes, thyroid function, and vitamin B12, are normal.
MRI of the brain shows generalized cortical atrophy most prominent in the hippocampi and temporal lobes, with no evidence of infarcts, masses, or hydrocephalus.
